_what: Which third-party code may appear where, and what it costs a consumer. One file because the two questions have one owner: a dependency is allowed only at a price we measured, and the price is what decides the place.
_who_reads_it: deps_gate.py (X2) enforces `allowed_paths`; the numbers are the evidence behind `verdict` and are re-measured by workspace/tools/x0_compile_cost.py, never typed by hand into prose.

budget.why: A public header is paid for by every consumer TU in their own build, on every platform, forever. 10% is the line above which 'we use library X internally' turns into 'we made the consumer's build 4x slower', and the plan says such a component may not appear on the public face.

measurement.statistic: median wall clock, first run discarded (cold page cache)
measurement.baseline: #include <foc/...> + main(), which is the same TU shape the `strict` gate compiles

etl.why_declared: Provenance for the parts of a motor controller that are easy to get subtly wrong and cheap to get from a tested, fielded embedded library: CRC (a wrong polynomial is silent), bit-stream packing for non-byte-aligned encoder frames, byte order, and fixed-capacity text formatting without allocation.
etl.what_it_buys: A second, independently written implementation to compare against our own on every push (the cross-check cases), and a tested bit manipulator behind the compiled face. It is evidence, not convenience: 'our CRC agrees with ETL byte for byte over 0..64 byte frames' is a sentence a reviewer can check.
etl.verdict: INTERNAL ONLY. Every candidate header costs a consumer 7x-34x the price of the whole foc include face, so ETL may not appear on any public header. It is a `cpp` bucket (conan) dependency, which is visible to the recipe, while `include/**` stays free of it: the include face is what a consumer actually pays for.

code_size._what: .text bytes for the same job done twice, -O2, same TU shape

crc16_ccitt.note: ETL is 10 bytes smaller: it is table driven, ours is bitwise. Neither is a reason on its own at this size; the cross-check is.

hex_format.note: A general format engine against `std::snprintf`, which lives in the C library either way. This is the one component whose size cost is real, and it is why nothing on the public face needs it.

gtest.why_declared: The test framework. Every case in test_package is written against it.

pybind11.why_declared: The Python consumer face (api/python_bindings.cpp). Optional: off unless enable_python_bindings.
